gloss: Blind people touching an elephant; signifies limited perspectives.
teaser: Ever wondered how a simple touch can lead to a big misunderstanding?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered how a simple touch can lead to a big misunderstanding? [break 1s] The phrase is: 盲人摸象, máng rén mō xiàng. [break 0.5s] 盲 (máng) - blind [break 0.5s] 人 (rén) - person [break 0.5s] 摸 (mō) - touch [break 0.5s] 象 (xiàng) - elephant [break 1s] So, 盲人摸象 literally means 'blind people touching an elephant' and figuratively refers to having a limited perspective on a situation. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] In ancient times, a group of blind men encountered an elephant for the first time. Each one touched a different part of the elephant's body, like the trunk, the ear, or the leg. Based on their limited experience, they each described the elephant differently, leading to a heated argument. This story illustrates how our limited views can lead us to misunderstand the bigger picture. [break 1.5s] Example 1: 他只看了报告的一部分，就认为项目很糟糕，这真是盲人摸象。 [break 1s] He only looked at part of the report and thought the project was terrible; this is truly 盲人摸象. [break 1s] Example 2: 你不能只听一个人的意见就下结论，这样就像盲人摸象。 [break 1s] You can't jump to conclusions based on just one person's opinion; that's like 盲人摸象. [break 1s] Example 3: 在讨论这个复杂的问题时，我们不能盲人摸象。 [break 1s] When discussing this complex issue, we can't be like 盲人摸象. [break 1s] So, remember 盲人摸象 means to have a limited perspective. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
